Empower Your Workplace From risk assessment and management to workplace training and business advancement, we’ll provide your team with the skills it needs to thrive. OUR SERVICES    Industry-leading Accreditations ISS is accredited with a number of national governing bodies positioning us as market leaders within the industries we work in. ACCREDITATIONS    Innovative Shared Services We are experts in the facilitation of workplace evolution, driven by a desire not only to empower our clients' workforces, but also to enhance their operations. ENQUIRE NOW   

What We Do

Learning and Development

ISS is a registered and accredited training and consulting company, aligned with a number of national bodies. We only employ fully accredited facilitators, assessors and moderators with real experience in their related industries, to ensure training and development of the highest quality. Training material is sector specific and can be customised according to client specific needs.

LEARN MORE

Legal and Regulatory Training

ISS’s legal and regulatory training programmes ensure that our clients comply with the legislation applicable to their specific business sector. This includes, but is not limited to, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, Driven Machinery Regulation, the Mining Act and Construction Regulations.

LEARN MORE

Risk Management

ISS offers comprehensive risk assessments in all business areas, incorporating strategic follow-up actions and controls, in line with accepted legal and regulatory frameworks. A digital platform developed by ISS Online will use technology to simplify, automate and fast-track all aspects of ongoing Risk Management, facilitating a more efficient process of Risk Identification, Evaluation and Quantification.

LEARN MORE

Business Advancement

The unrelenting rate of change in today’s fast-moving economic environment will increasingly demand agility from businesses. More than ever, organisations will need to embrace change and implement their own advancement to stay abreast of it. Failure to do so could cost them their competitive edge, or even compromise their ability to meet customer needs long term.

LEARN MORE

Service Coverage

With an ever-expanding network of branches and agents, ISS prides itself on a formidable footprint across Southern Africa and the ability to ‘be wherever our clients are’.

As a business that empowers workplaces, we’re showcasing Africa’s capacity, and creating a blueprint for the success of a new generation of leaders.

Who We Are

BEE Level 1

Innovative Shared Services is proud to be a BBBEE Level 1 contributor, to add to our extensive range of accreditations and certifications.

Vision

Innovative Shared Services strives to be a truly African company, embracing continuous improvement and learning.

This will be achieved through leveraging the quality of our people, products and customer service that brings sustainable growth, improved shareholder value and upliftment to society. We embrace a dynamic view of our changing world; our ambition is to be the catalyst of change for a whole generation, a beacon of leadership and courage.

Mission

Our mission will be achieved through an investment in people, developing human potential, creating systems that allow growth and a leadership style that is participative yet decisive.

Modes of Delivery

Face to Face

At ISS, we appreciate the value that face-to-face engagement adds to the South African workplace. We have dedicated and qualified individuals who successfully deliver our services through Face-to-Face interventions throughout all our business units and related service offerings.

Digital

At ISS, we embrace technology and have digitised every aspect of our business. We have a team of highly-skilled experts including Software Developers, eLearning Mentors and Subject Matter Experts. Our team strives to support our users to optimise their online experience – through all our business units.

Our Accreditations

ISS is accredited with a number of national governing bodies (SETAs and the QCTO) which allows us not only to participate in complex work tasks, but also positions us as market leaders within the many industries we work in.

Our Difference

Total Service Approach

Our approach to employee development and business sustainability is creative, carefully planned and, above all, productive.

Ever-Expanding Network

ISS has built up a formidable footprint across Southern Africa, and is proud of its ability to ‘be wherever our clients are’.

Accreditation Excellence

ISS only employs fully-accredited facilitators and assessors with experience in their related industries to ensure training and development of the highest quality.

Expertise and Experience

ISS has broad exposure and an incredibly good track record in servicing clients across an array of markets and economic sectors.

A Proven Track Record

ISS is a dynamic team that has satisfied over 1000 customers, and continues to innovate by offering an array of diverse, strategic training and development solutions to large corporates and SMEs alike.

A Bespoke Approach

We understand that every client has unique requirements. At the very core of our business, we approach each project with the care and attention it needs.

item.description:
• The Procurement Trap: An economic perspective on the draft general public procurement regulations
    July 20, 2026
    Written by Professor Johan Fourie, Chair of Economics, History and Policy at Stellenbosch University, this CDE Viewpoints report assesses the draft General Public Procurement Regulations and argues that South Africa’s procurement system needs stronger institutional capacity rather than more complex regulation.
  • CDE Submission | Buying Badly: How the draft procurement regulations will raise costs and deepen corruption
    July 16, 2026
    CDE called on National Treasury to reconsider and withdraw the preferential procurement provisions in its draft public procurement regulations. The core preferential procurement mechanisms in the regulations – set-asides, prequalification and compulsory subcontracting – are likely to increase the cost of everything the state buys, delay delivery and create new opportunities for corruption.
  • Andres Velasco in conversation with Ann Bernstein
    July 14, 2026
    Ann Bernstein recently interviewed Andrés Velasco, Dean of the LSE’s School of Public Policy, to discuss how the London Consensus (a new book on economic principles for the 21st century) differs from the earlier, influential Washington Consensus and what South Africa should learn from it.

    How we promote solutions

    The decisions of those in power directly impact the lives of all South Africans.

    Government decisions can grow opportunity or smother it. They can create wealth or destroy it. They can expand freedom or erode it.

    The IRR holds those in power accountable. We fight against bad decisions. We promote solutions that make life in South Africa better for all.

    Our community and track record

    12 000

    Friends of the IRR

    500 000

    Subscribers

    1 000+

    Articles per year

    90+

    Years fighting
    for freedom

    With their monthly donations of R80-R150, the Friends of the IRR allow us to oppose bad ideas, policies, and decisions, and put forward real solutions.
    Thousands of South Africans subscribe to the podcasts, video channels, social media platforms and e-mail newsletters of our operational units to stay in touch with our work.
    Every day, we publish opinion pieces, letters and articles to inform the public debate and provide classically liberal commentary on current issues.
    For almost a century, the IRR has exerted influence, shaped public debate, defeated bad policies, and stood for a free, non-racial, and prosperous South Africa for all. We proudly continue doing so.

    About the IRR

    We conduct research, promote policy solutions, and fight for freedom, equality of opportunity, and the rights of every individual.

    We stand for classical liberalism - an effective way to defeat poverty and tyranny through a system of limited government, a market economy, private enterprise, freedom of speech, individual liberty, property rights, and the rule of law.

    Find out more

    Our research

    We are proud to carry on the IRR’s legacy of high-quality research. Our SA Survey (published annually since 1948) provides comprehensive data on all aspects of SA society. Our books, reports, policy papers, and parliamentary submissions offer in-depth analysis of South Africa's challenges and practical, pro-freedom solutions.

    If you believe that our country can overcome its challenges with the right policies and decisions, we’re on your side.

About the DPRU

The DPRU is a university-recognised research unit within the School of Economics at the University of Cape Town. We conduct policy-relevant socio-economic research in the fields of labour markets, poverty and inequality.
Read more

DPRU Publications

The DPRU publishes numerous scholarly outputs representing socioeconomic research: a Working Paper series, Policy Briefs, Fact Sheets, journal articles, chapters in books and others.
Read more

Welcome to the Development Policy Research Unit

The Development Policy Research Unit (DPRU) is one of Africa's premier economic policy think tanks. The DPRU aims to inform economic policymaking through specialising in academically rigorous research encompassing the socio-economic challenges in South Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa.  Specifically, the DPRU cognate areas range from labour market analysis, growth, poverty and inequality dynamics through to areas such as economic complexity analysis and regulation and governance. 

The DPRU is a university-recognized research unit located within the School of Economics at the University of Cape Town, and has been actively engaged in policy-relevant socio-economic research for nearly 30 years, establishing itself as one of South Africa’s premier research institutions in the field.

Through the application of economic and statistical techniques, our aim is to produce academically credible and rigorous policy analysis.The three core objectives of the Unit are to:

  • foster high quality, policy relevant research within the DPRU
  • train a new generation of research economists within the Unit, and
  • disseminate knowledge to decision- and policy-makers in government, the private sector and civil society.
